title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting and streaming stability
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with OpenAI's behavior for request params (top_p, temperature, presence/ frequency penalties), explicit role handling (system/user/assistant), stop token handling, optional logprobs output, and deterministic response formatting when streaming. Additionally address a class of streaming stability bugs where partial chunks produced malformed JSON for structured outputs.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add full params mapping and validation for chat.completions (top_p, temperature, penalties)
fix(streaming): stabilize chunk framing to avoid truncated JSON for structured outputs
feat(api): support roles mapping and explicit system role precedence in compatibility layer
feat(logprobs): wire up logprobs generation path and opt-out via request param
docs: update openai compatibility docs and examples for stop sequences and formatting
review_comments: Liam Chen (2026-02-21): Great work. Two requests: add deterministic ordering for role->channel mapping in the compatibility layer and add a unit test for stop sequence edge-cases (overlapping tokens).
Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): Addressed: added deterministic sort for roles mapping and new unit tests for overlapping stop sequences. PTAL.

Priya Nair (2026-02-23): Found a flake in streaming tests where small buffers produced truncated JSON for structured outputs. Can you ensure chunk boundaries never split multi-byte UTF-8 characters and add an integration test?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-24): Fix applied in frame_builder to respect UTF-8 boundaries and to emit partial token escapes. Added integration test and a stress benchmark script.
Marco Diaz (2026-02-25): Left a nit about a log message and requested a short docs paragraph to explain the stop-sequence precedence with system vs user roles.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-26): Nits fixed, expanded docs and added a short section on stop sequence precedence. Ready to merge.
release_notes: Feature: OpenAI-compliant /v1/chat.completions parameter handling (top_p, temperature, presence/frequency penalties), explicit role precedence (system/user/assistant), support for stop sequences matching OpenAI semantics, optional logprobs output, and improvements to streaming stability and structured output formatting. Includes docs and examples.
